text: Case Number from the OSHA Log
Injury Description - Describe Activities of Employee When Injury or Illness Occurred and What Tools, Machinery, Objects, Chemicals, Etc. Were Involved.
answer: Employee was lifting and moving boxes of printed brochures (approximately 35 lbs each) from a waist-high storage rack to a rolling cart for an offsite client meeting. A box, metal storage rack, and a two-shelf cart were involved. While repositioning a box onto the cart, employee twisted at the waist to avoid a coworker passing behind.

text: What Happened to Cause This Injury or Illness? (Describe How The Injury Occurred)
answer: While turning to set a 35-lb box onto a cart, employee rotated her torso without moving her feet, resulting in an acute twisting motion and immediate sharp pain in the lower back. No slip or fall occurred; injury was due to overexertion and awkward posture while lifting.

text: What Was The Injury or Illness? (State the Part of Body Affected and How It Was Affected)
answer: Lumbar strain to the lower back musculature with localized pain, muscle spasm, and limited range of motion. No radiating numbness reported. Treated conservatively with rest, NSAIDs, and light-duty recommendation.
